english.title: Make a false claim for a drawback / allowance / remission payment with intent to fraud
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), with intent to defraud His Majesty, obtained for

(A)_[yourself]_
(B)_[another person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..),]_

an amount, namely **(..SPECIFY AMOUNT..), by way of drawback, allowance, remission or repayment of, or any rebate from, any duty in respect of goods which was

(C)_[not lawfully payable or allowable in respect thereof]_
(D)_[greater than the amount so payable or allowable]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 136(1) and (2) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.

english.notes: Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding £20,000 or three times the value of the goods involved, whichever is the greater.
Indictment: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions
20 years
